name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
best_time: June-September for the flooded forest; winter for dry trails
short_description: Ratargul, on the Louhajang beel in Tangail, is Bangladesh's best-known flooded forest - a boat glide into green tunnel-water that is genuinely special in monsoon. It is the standard eco day trip on the Dhaka-Tangail road.

long_description:
Ratargul, on the Louhajang beel in Tangail, is Bangladesh's best-known flooded forest - a boat glide into green tunnel-water that is genuinely special in monsoon. It is the standard eco day trip on the Dhaka-Tangail road. A freshwater swamp forest flooded each monsoon, where country boats glide under krishnachur and kadam canopy along the Dingonataha channel. Run as an eco-tourism site with a forest department; boat hire is mandatory in the flooded months and there is a small canteen and camping point.

On the ground: Boat entry into a drowned forest; Krishnachur and kadam canopy; Forest-department eco-tourism site; Camping and bonfire evenings; Ninety minutes from Dhaka via Tongabari. GHORA GHURI guides rate the eco, river, forest character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Natore's rajbari is one of the great landlord houses of Bengal - a palace, tank, temples and guest wings belonging to the rajas who once ruled a quarter of north Bengal. Rajshahi is forty minutes away and the site is easy. The palace of the Rajas of Natore, rebuilt in 1860s Indo-European style, with a huge water tank, a guest house, and the Jagannath temple of the original estate. The palace museum keeps royal portraits, silverware and furniture; the garden, the Dhanbhandar and the palace gateway are the photographic core.

Godagari turns Rajshahi into a river city: ghats, ferries, mango orchards on the Barind edge and the wide Padma. long_description:
Gaur was the seat of sultanate Bengal and remains one of Asia's great archaeological cities, much of it still unexcavated. From Choto Sona Mosque to the Rangpur-side gateways, it is the deepest history day in the country and the least visited. The medieval capital of Bengal, Gaur-Lakhnauti, spreads mosques, gates and mints across two countries; its Choto Sona Mosque carries the only surviving marble veneer of a sultanate mosque in Bangladesh. The Kotuali gateway, the Darasbari Mosque, the mint mound and the Rohanpur border are all within a thirty-minute loop on decent road.

On the ground: Choto Sona Mosque in white marble; Darasbari and Tantipara mosques; Kotuali gate of the royal city; Rohanpur land port nearby; Mango-and-date orchards en route. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, world-heritage-candidate, architecture character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

name: Zinda Pir's Mazar & Dhap
best_time: Any month; Thursday evening and the annual jatra are busiest
short_description: Rangpur's Zinda Pir dargah at Laksamibazar is the city's devotional heart, and its fair preserved jatra, mani-raj and puppet traditions that have died elsewhere. It pairs with the museum and Tajhat for a gentle half day.
short_bn: লক্ষ্মীবাজারে 'জিন্দা পীর'-এর মাজার রংপুরের আধ্যাত্মিক কেন্দ্র; বার্ষিক যাত্রা মেলায় মণিরাজ, যাত্রা আর পুতুলনাচ প্রজন্ম ধরে টিকে আছে। জাদুঘর-তাজহাটের সঙ্গে সহজ আধা দিন।
long_description:
Rangpur's Zinda Pir dargah at Laksamibazar is the city's devotional heart, and its fair preserved jatra, mani-raj and puppet traditions that have died elsewhere. It pairs with the museum and Tajhat for a gentle half day. The shrine of the 'living saint' of Rangpur, beside the Dhapa mound, whose annual jatra for generations drew performers and traders from half of north Bengal. The mazar, the old pond and the fairground are a ten-minute walk from the museum; modest dress and weekday timing make photography respectful.

On the ground: Century-old dargah and pond; Annual jatra with jhul and manishi; Rangpur's oldest public gathering space; Within walking distance of the museum; Langa-bandhan folk traditions. GHORA GHURI guides rate the pilgrimage, heritage, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Zinda Pir's Mazar & Dhap: Rangpur is 6-7 hours by bus via Bangla-Bandor, or the Rangpur Express overnight train. Air: no airport; Parbatipur railway junction, about 1 hour, is the rail gateway. Ground links run through Rangpur bus stand, with shared vans to Nilphamari, Lalmonirhat and Thakurgaon.

Staying over: expect hotel blocks near Dhap at Dhamirphula, plus circuit houses for groups.

Planning notes: the season window is Any month; Thursday evening and the annual jatra are busiest. Budget 100-500 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Dress modestly, keep phones away during prayer, and check festival dates - crowds can double transport and hotel prices overnight.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with Zinda Pir's Mazar & Dhap site authorities before travel. name: Tajhat Palace
best_time: October-March; the museum is closed on Sundays
short_description: Tajhat Palace, built for Maharaja Priya Lal Roy, is north Bengal's grandest landlord house and now the region's best museum. Its columns, galleries and lawns make a complete morning within twenty minutes of the town centre.
short_bn: প্রিয় লাল রায়ের ১৯০২ সালের তাজহাট প্রাসাদ উত্তর বাংলার জমিদার স্থাপত্যের শিখর, এখন বিভাগীয় জাদুঘর — ইতালীয় স্তম্ভ, ভাস্কর্য গ্যালারি আর চওড়া বারান্দা।
long_description:
Tajhat Palace, built for Maharaja Priya Lal Roy, is north Bengal's grandest landlord house and now the region's best museum. Its columns, galleries and lawns make a complete morning within twenty minutes of the town centre. A 1902 Italian-columned zamindan palace that now runs as the Rangpur Divisional Museum, with restored plasterwork, a central hall and a sculpture gallery. The palace gardens, the Cane-chandni block and the terracotta-age relics inside make two comfortable hours; the Zinda Pir mazar is five minutes away.

On the ground: Italian and Corinthian colonnades; Restored durbar and guest halls; Sculpture and terracotta galleries; Garden, gate and carriage porch; Divisional museum since 1988. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, museum, architecture character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Tajhat Palace: Rangpur is 6-7 hours by bus via Bangla-Bandor, or the Rangpur Express overnight train. Air: no airport; Parbatipur railway junction, about 1 hour, is the rail gateway. Ground links run through Rangpur bus stand, with shared vans to Nilphamari, Lalmonirhat and Thakurgaon.

Staying over: expect hotel blocks near Dhap at Dhamirphula, plus circuit houses for groups.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; the museum is closed on Sundays. Budget 200-800 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Bring water, a hat and patience: most brick monuments are open, shaded by little more than their own arcades, and a guide reads the site far better than any plaque.

best_time: October-March; mornings for the courtyard light
short_description: Kadamatali, near the India border at Thakurgaon, is one of the best restored zamindan palaces in the country, now alive with exhibitions and cultural evenings. It anchors a Rangpur-division heritage route that few foreigners have ever driven.
short_bn: ঠাকুরগাঁয়ের কাদামতলী রাজবাড়ি উনিশ শতকের জমিদার প্রাসাদের সংস্কারকৃত উদাহরণ — কেন্দ্রীয় উঠোন, খিলান-বারান্দা, প্রদর্শনী আর সাংস্কৃতিক সন্ধ্যা; সীমান্তের কাছে বিমোহিত ঐতিহ্য পথ।
long_description:
Kadamatali, near the India border at Thakurgaon, is one of the best restored zamindan palaces in the country, now alive with exhibitions and cultural evenings. It anchors a Rangpur-division heritage route that few foreigners have ever driven. A late-nineteenth-century zamindan palace with a central courtyard, Greek-style verandahs and a guest house, restored as a cultural centre after a long decay. Thakurgaon's Tetulia mosque, the Ranachandi hillock and the Dukhcha reservoir are all within thirty minutes, making this a hub rather than a single stop.

name: Ranachandi Temple & Hill
best_time: October-March; Chaitra Sankranti mela in April
short_description: Ranachandi is a modest hill that reads like a mountain in the flat north - a temple, a fair ground and a sal forest above Thakurgaon's fields. It gives Rangpur division the hill-walk element travellers look for elsewhere.
short_bn: ঠাকুরগাঁয়ের রণচণ্ডী সমতলের ওপর উঠে থাকা টিলা — চাঁদিনী মন্দির, চৈত্র মেলা আর শালবনের পথ; রংপুর বিভাগে পাহাড়ের অনুভূতি পাওয়ার একমাত্র সহজ ঠিকানা।
long_description:
Ranachandi is a modest hill that reads like a mountain in the flat north - a temple, a fair ground and a sal forest above Thakurgaon's fields. It gives Rangpur division the hill-walk element travellers look for elsewhere. The highest point in Thakurgaon district, a low hill of sal and mahua with a Chandini temple, reached by a forest road from Ranishankar. The 1790-era temple, the annual mela, the viewpoint over the plains and the surrounding forest patches make a half-day with the border towns.

On the ground: Hilltop temple and open viewpoint; Forest road and sal patches; Annual Chaitra mela and fairground; Deer and python habitat reports; Border-country village lanes. best_time: November-February; monsoon for the full reservoir
short_description: Dukhcha gives Thakurgaon its recreation shore - a wide reservoir with a bund walk, boats, picnic grass and winter birds. It is an easy add-on to Kadamatali and the Ranachandi hill within a single afternoon loop.

long_description:

The bund walk, the forest check posts and the small amusement zone handle families; birders should come for the winter waterfowl and raptors over the water.

best_time: October-March; the site is open and shaded little
short_description: Bhitargarh, near Panchagarh, is one of Bengal's largest and least-visited ancient forts - a ring of rampart and mound landscape that locals tie to the Kokilanka of legend. The Teesta, the nilkuthis and the zero point complete the day.
short_bn: পঞ্চগড়ের ভীমরগড় বাংলার বৃহত্তম প্রাচীন দুর্গচিহ্নগুলোর একটি — ২৮ কিমি পরিখা-বেষ্টিত ইট-মাটির স্তর, কিংবদন্তির কোকিলংকা নগর। তিস্তা আর নীলকুঠির সঙ্গে এক দিন।
long_description:
Bhitargarh, near Panchagarh, is one of Bengal's largest and least-visited ancient forts - a ring of rampart and mound landscape that locals tie to the Kokilanka of legend. The Teesta, the nilkuthis and the zero point complete the day. A rampart circuit said to run some twenty-eight kilometres across Bangladesh and India, linked in local tradition to the Kokilanka of the epics. Excavated gates, a carved stone pillar and brick mounds sit in fields near Panchagarh; the zero point on the Teesta is twenty minutes north.

On the ground: Twenty-eight km of earthen rampart; Cross-border archaeological park; Carved stone pillar and gates; Mounds with Kush-Gupta era brick; Twenty minutes from Panchagarh town. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, archaeology, border character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Staying over: expect riverside resorts on the Teesta bank, plus town guesthouses near Zero Point.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; the site is open and shaded little. Budget 300-1,000 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Two days here cost less than a day on the south-eastern coast. Bangladesh's northernmost river shoreline, where the Teesta runs wide and shallow past resorts, boat points and a sandbar that appears each winter. The zero-point border view, the tea gardens of the northern tract and the winter river-sand picnics are the standard circuit from Panchagarh.

A revered Sufi shrine in the Char Dargaramia of Gaibandha, whose annual urs draws a huge gathering across the Jamuna char belt. Access is via flood-plain roads and small ferries; plan for a slow approach and stay with a local family rather than hunting for hotels.

name: Muktagachha Zamindan Baris
best_time: October-March; Chaitra Sankranti mela in April
short_description: Muktagachha keeps one of Bengal's densest zamindan townships - palaces, temples, a tank and a fair that has outlived the family's power. It is the standout heritage stop in Mymensingh division and an easy overnight from Dhaka.
short_bn: মুক্তাগাছায় আটানী, কমলা রানী ও বাঁধচিপের জমিদার প্রাসাদ, মন্দির আর বিশাল পুকুর — শতাব্দীপ্রাচীন চৈত্র সংক্রান্তির মেলাসহ বাংলায় জমিদার পাড়ার সবচেয়ে ঘন সমাহার।
long_description:
Muktagachha keeps one of Bengal's densest zamindan townships - palaces, temples, a tank and a fair that has outlived the family's power. It is the standout heritage stop in Mymensingh division and an easy overnight from Dhaka. The Atani, Komola Rani and Bawnchhip palaces of the Muktagachha rajas - a cluster of brick zamindan houses, temples and tanks with an annual fair that has run for centuries. Much of the fabric is restored by the department and by families who still live inside it; the fair ground and the palace tank are the pulse of the visit.

On the ground: Komola Rani palace and temple; Atani Rajbari and guest house; Great palace tank and ghats; Chaitra Sankranti mela and jatra; Ninety minutes from Mymensingh town. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, village, photography character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Muktagachha Zamindan Baris: Mymensingh is 2.5-3.5 hours via the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway or the Tamabil bus. Air: no airport; Shahjalal (Dhaka) is the practical gateway 2.5 hours away. Ground links run through Mymensingh bus stand and railway junction on the north-east line.

Staying over: expect hotels on Airport Road, university guest houses and Dakurghat cottages.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; Chaitra Sankranti mela in April. Budget 250-900 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Bring water, a hat and patience: most brick monuments are open, shaded by little more than their own arcades, and a guide reads the site far better than any plaque.

best_time: October-March; closed Sundays
short_description: Shashi Lodge gives Mymensingh town its best single monument - a nineteenth-century royal chateau in brick, with a museum of sculpture and terracotta from the district's ruined temples, thirty minutes from the airport road.

best_time: October-March; the winter fair is the liveliest week
short_description: Pagla's Adishur temple ties Mymensingh to the pan-Bengali legend of the five Brahmins brought from Kannauj, and its annual fair still draws pilgrims across district lines. A short, unusual heritage stop between the town and Muktagachha.
short_bn: পাগলার আদিশূর মন্দির কান্যকুব্জের পাঁচ ব্রাহ্মণের কিংবদন্তির সঙ্গে জড়িত উত্তর বাংলার প্রাচীন তীর্থ; মাঘের মেলা আজও দুই জেলার যাত্রী টানে।
long_description:

A short, unusual heritage stop between the town and Muktagachha. The shrine of Adishur, the legendary fifth-century Brahmin priest of Kannauj, is one of the oldest continuously venerated Hindu sites in northern Bengal. The temple fair attracts pilgrims from across the Mymensingh-Brahmanbaria axis, and the Brahmanbaria-side Adishur shrine shares the same legend.

name: Jangalbari & Egarosindur Forts
best_time: November-February; the Baro-Bhuiyan history walk
short_description: Kishoreganj preserves the strongholds of the Baro-Bhuiyan rajas who resisted Mughal annexation - Jangalbari and Egarosindur, brick ramparts and tanks in open country. It is the best history field trip within three hours of Dhaka.
short_bn: কিশোরগঞ্জে মূসা খাঁর জঙ্গলবাড়ি আর এগারোসিন্দুর ইটের দুর্গ-প্রাসাদ, বারো ভুঁইয়ার মুঘল-প্রতিরোধের সাক্ষী; ভাটরশালীতে ইসা খাঁর সমাধিও সেই দিনেই।
long_description:
Kishoreganj preserves the strongholds of the Baro-Bhuiyan rajas who resisted Mughal annexation - Jangalbari and Egarosindur, brick ramparts and tanks in open country. It is the best history field trip within three hours of Dhaka. Two of the fortress-palaces of Musa Khan of Bhapol, the Baro-Bhuiyan chief who fought the Mughals, standing four kilometres apart in Kishoreganj's fields. Isa Khan's tomb at Bhatrashali and the local museums complete the picture of the twelve landlords of Bhapol, under three hours from Dhaka via Tangail or the Padma side.

On the ground: Musa Khan's Jangalbari rampart; Egarosindur palace and treasury mound; Isa Khan's tomb at Bhatrashali; Baro-Bhuiyan war history; Kishoreganj bus stand as base. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, village, offbeat character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Jangalbari & Egarosindur Forts: Kishoreganj is 3-4 hours via Tongabari or the Dhaka-Sylhet highway at Ashuganj side. Air: no airport; Osmani (Sylhet) is roughly 1.5 hours by road. Ground links run through Kishoreganj bus stand; rickshaw and vans to Egarosindur and Jangalbari.

Staying over: expect a few hotels in Sadar - most visitors return to Dhaka or Sylhet the same day.

short_description: Sarakhola is the north-east's least commercialised hill country - bamboo ridges, river views and village stays an hour beyond Kishoreganj. Trekkers who find Sylhet too developed come here, and return with worse photos and better stories.

long_description:
Sarakhola is the north-east's least commercialised hill country - bamboo ridges, river views and village stays an hour beyond Kishoreganj. Trekkers who find Sylhet too developed come here, and return with worse photos and better stories. A chain of bamboo-covered hillocks above the Dhonapani river in eastern Kishoreganj, with a Khasi-influenced border culture, orchids and a winter mist line. Local guides run the ridgeline walks and the Boli points; there are no hotels, so homestays and a tent stay at Sarakhola high school ground are the standard.

On the ground: Bamboo and orchid ridge walks; Dhonapani river valley viewpoints; Khasi and Garo border villages; Winter mist over the treeline; Zero commercial resort footprint. GHORA GHURI guides rate the hill, eco, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Staying over: expect a few hotels in Sadar - most visitors return to Dhaka or Sylhet the same day.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; monsoon for green, winter for trekking. Budget 1,200-3,200 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 2 day(s) on the ground. long_description:
Jamalpur's Shah Jamal dargah is one of the oldest Islamic shrines of north-central Bengal, and its annual Urs remains the district's biggest gathering. Add the Baishteri church and Dayamoyee temple and the half day is complete. The patron shrine that gave Jamalpur its name, on the Brahmaputra bank, with a mosque, a tank and a three-day Urs fair. The adjacent Gandi ghat, the Dayamoyee temple and the Baishteri railway junction make a half day in a district most travellers only cross.

On the ground: Sufi shrine of the 14th century; Riverside ghat and boat culture; Adjacent historic mosque and tank; Urs fair with rural mela; Gateway to Madhupur and Baishteri. The Gandhi Ashram at Baishteri, where the 1920s non-cooperation work ran, and the old sugar-mill township of Zeal Bangla lie within minutes.

name: Dhobaura China Clay Hills
best_time: November-February; after rain for the colour contrast
short_description: The Dhobaura china-clay hills look lunar and are completely unmanaged - a working excavation landscape beside the Madhupur tract. Photographers and off-road travellers have made it the most photographed surprise in Mymensingh division.
short_bn: ময়মনসিংহ-নেত্রকোণা সীমান্তের ধোবাউরার চিনামাটির টিলা — হাতে খোঁড়া সাদা-গেরুয়া খনিজ ভূমি, বৃষ্টির পানিতে টার্কোয়াজ হ্রদ; মধুপুর গড়ের কিনারায় অবাস্তব এক দৃশ্য।
long_description:
The Dhobaura china-clay hills look lunar and are completely unmanaged - a working excavation landscape beside the Madhupur tract. Photographers and off-road travellers have made it the most photographed surprise in Mymensingh division. Pitted white-and-ochre china-clay hills on the Mymensingh-Netrokona border, dug by hand for the ceramics trade and now an accidental landscape photographers keep finding. Madhupur's forest edge, the Someswari river and the Dhobaura haor belt lie within thirty minutes, making a genuine off-beat circuit.

On the ground: Sculpted white clay excavations; Turquoise rain-filled pits; Hand-digging craft of the region; Sunset over the terraced scarps; Combine with Madhupur Garh. GHORA GHURI guides rate the offbeat, eco, photography character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Dhobaura China Clay Hills: Mymensingh is 2.5-3.5 hours via the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway or the Tamabil bus. Air: no airport; Shahjalal (Dhaka) is the practical gateway 2.5 hours away. Ground links run through Mymensingh bus stand and railway junction on the north-east line.

Staying over: expect hotels on Airport Road, university guest houses and Dakurghat cottages.

name: Cox's Bazar Sea Beach
best_time: October-March; monsoon swim bans run June-September
short_description: Cox's Bazar is Bangladesh's default seaside escape: a very long, very flat beach of gentle surf, resort hotels, crab stalls and day trips to Himchari. Book midweek in winter, avoid monsoon swimming, and allow three days to see past the first strip.
short_bn: প্রায় ১২০ কিলোমিটার দীর্ঘ বিশ্বের বৃহত্তম প্রাকৃতিক সমুদ্র সৈকত — লাবণী, কলাতলী, সুগন্ধা সেক্টর, হিমছড়ি-ইনানী দিনভ্রমণ আর কাঁটামাছের দোকান; শীতে সপ্তাহের মাঝের দিন বুক করাই বুদ্ধিমানের কাজ।
long_description:
Cox's Bazar is Bangladesh's default seaside escape: a very long, very flat beach of gentle surf, resort hotels, crab stalls and day trips to Himchari. Book midweek in winter, avoid monsoon swimming, and allow three days to see past the first strip. At roughly 120 km it is the longest continuous natural sea beach on earth, open at both ends so sunrise and sunset both land on the sand. Laboni is the patrolled, swimmable stretch with the resort strip behind it, while Khuni Pahaar and the headland cafes are where repeat visitors spend their evenings.

On the ground: 120 km continuous tidal beach; Laboni, Kolatoli and Sugandha sectors; Himchari and Inani day trips; Seafood markets and dried-fish lanes; Beach-drive hotel strip. GHORA GHURI guides rate the beach, family, photography character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Cox's Bazar Sea Beach: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; monsoon swim bans run June-September. Budget 4,500-16,000 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 3 day(s) on the ground. Sea conditions matter more than the calendar here - the surf is calm and swimmable only outside the monsoon, and tides decide how much sand is usable.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with Cox's Bazar Sea Beach site authorities before travel. short_description: Himchari pairs a rough, beautiful beach with a monsoon waterfall and hill-top viewpoints inside a national park, half an hour north of Cox's Bazar. It is the standard first day-trip for beach guests and works well for photography at either end of the day.
short_bn: পাহাড় যেখানে সমুদ্রে নেমে এসেছে — হিমছড়িতে ক্লিফটপ সৈকত, জাতীয় উদ্যানের ঝরনা, আকাশধুঁয়া লেক আর শূন্যবিন্দুর দৃশ্য, কক্সবাজার থেকে চল্লিশ মিনিট।
long_description:
Himchari pairs a rough, beautiful beach with a monsoon waterfall and hill-top viewpoints inside a national park, half an hour north of Cox's Bazar. It is the standard first day-trip for beach guests and works well for photography at either end of the day. Where the hills fall straight into the sea: a cliff-top beach, a freshwater cascade inside a national park and a zero-point view over the Bay. Akahu Lake and the waterfall cave are short walks from the park gate; the road from Cox's Bazar is paved and takes about forty minutes by CNG.

On the ground: Clifftop beach with waterfall nearby; Himchari National Park trails; Akahu Lake and Madhabchari temple; Zero Point viewpoint over the bay; Wildest surf on the Cox's Bazar coast. GHORA GHURI guides rate the beach, hill, waterfall character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Himchari: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; July-September for full waterfall volume. Budget 600-2,200 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Sea conditions matter more than the calendar here - the surf is calm and swimmable only outside the monsoon, and tides decide how much sand is usable.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with Himchari site authorities before travel. name: Inani Beach & Longu Beach
best_time: November-March; low tide exposes the coral flats
short_description: Inani trades the resort strip for coral shelves, tidal islets and empty sand an hour south of Cox's Bazar. It is the right choice for a half-day of quiet wading and seafood in the fishing village, especially on weekdays.
short_bn: কক্সবাজারের এক ঘণ্টা দক্ষিণে ইনানী — জোয়ার ভাটায় খোলা প্রবালপৃষ্ঠ, পাথুরে পুকুর, নির্জন বালুচর আর লংগুর জেলেপাড়া; রিসর্টের ভিড় এড়ানোর ঠিকানা।
long_description:
Inani trades the resort strip for coral shelves, tidal islets and empty sand an hour south of Cox's Bazar. It is the right choice for a half-day of quiet wading and seafood in the fishing village, especially on weekdays. An eleven-kilometre beach of exposed coral and tidal islets south of Cox's Bazar, calm enough at low water for wading among the rock pools. Longu Beach, a short ride further, has the fishing-village frontage and the better sunset; both are reachable by motorbike or shared van from Palongkhali.

On the ground: Coral and rock-pool flats at low tide; Eleven km of quiet sand; Longu Beach fishing-village life; Cheap motorbike access from Palongkhali; No resort strip, bring supplies. GHORA GHURI guides rate the beach, island, offbeat character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Inani Beach & Longu Beach: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

Planning notes: the season window is November-March; low tide exposes the coral flats. Budget 500-1,800 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Sea conditions matter more than the calendar here - the surf is calm and swimmable only outside the monsoon, and tides decide how much sand is usable.

name: Sugandha Beach & Khuni Pahaar
best_time: October-March; nights are cool and clear in December
short_description: Sugandha and Khuni Pahaar are the active end of Cox's Bazar - surf lessons, headland walks, tent nights on the sand and none of the Kolatoli traffic. A good half day for travellers who find the main beach too built up.
short_bn: কক্সবাজার রেখার উত্তর প্রান্ত সুগন্ধা-খুনি পাহাড় — বোর্ডিং, পাহাড়ি চূড়া, বালুচরে তাঁবুর রাত আর কলাতলীর যানজটমুক্ত বিকেল।
long_description:
Sugandha and Khuni Pahaar are the active end of Cox's Bazar - surf lessons, headland walks, tent nights on the sand and none of the Kolatoli traffic. A good half day for travellers who find the main beach too built up. The northern end of the Cox's Bazar beach line, where the sand curves under a low forested headland and the surf is strong enough for bodyboarding. Surf schools and campfire operators work this stretch in winter; the headland walk takes an hour and ends at a lookout over Teknaf bay.

On the ground: Bodyboarding and beginner surf; Khuni Pahaar headland and lookout; Beach-campfire and tent nights; Sunrise walks on empty sand; Quiet hotels off the main strip. name: Moheshwar & Dariapasha, Maheshkhali
best_time: October-March; ferry tide matters for the crossing
short_description: Maheshkhali gives Cox's Bazar travellers a different coast: a causeway island of shrimp ponds, a hilltop Shiva temple and quiet tidal beaches, reachable on a thirty-minute ferry. It suits a two-wheel day trip more than an overnight.
short_bn: কক্সবাজারের ফেরি-দ্বীপ মহেশখালী — চিংড়িঘের, ধীরে-ঢালা পাহাড়ে শিবমন্দির আর দরিয়াপাশার সমতল সৈকত; সাইকেল-বাইকের এক দিনের জন্য আদর্শ।
long_description:
Maheshkhali gives Cox's Bazar travellers a different coast: a causeway island of shrimp ponds, a hilltop Shiva temple and quiet tidal beaches, reachable on a thirty-minute ferry. It suits a two-wheel day trip more than an overnight. An island of tidal creeks and shrimp farms thirty minutes by ferry from Cox's Bazar, keeping a cliff-top Shiva temple at Moheshwar and a beach at Dariapasha. The island is joined to the mainland by a causeway with boat points; the cyclone-shelter belt and the Kutubdia-side sandbank make it a full-day loop.

On the ground: Cliff temple of Shiva at Moheshwar; Dariapasha's flat, safe swimming; Cox's Bazar ferry crossing at Maitkhali; Shrimp-farm and village cycling lanes; Cyclone-shelter heritage landscape. GHORA GHURI guides rate the island, beach, pilgrimage character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Moheshwar & Dariapasha, Maheshkhali: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; ferry tide matters for the crossing. Budget 700-2,200 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Everything arrives by boat, including supplies. Carry cash, expect early power cuts after midnight, and never plan a same-day return in uncertain weather.

name: Teknaf Town & Shah Parbat
best_time: November-March; the launch to St. Martin's leaves from here
short_description: Teknaf is the frontier town that funnels everyone to St. Martin's, and rewards those who stay: a border river, a hilltop dargah over the sea, and markets where Cox's Bazar prices halve. One night here beats a rushed island round trip.
short_bn: সেন্ট মার্টিনের লঞ্চঘাট টেকনাফ সীমান্তের শহর — নাফ নদীর পাড়, শাহ পীরের টিলা-মাজার আর সস্তার মাছবাজার; দ্বীপে তাড়াহুড়ো না করে এখানে এক রাত থাকা ভালো।
long_description:
Teknaf is the frontier town that funnels everyone to St. Martin's, and rewards those who stay: a border river, a hilltop dargah over the sea, and markets where Cox's Bazar prices halve. One night here beats a rushed island round trip. Bangladesh's south-eastern tip, where the Naf river marks the Myanmar border, and the shrine of Shah Muhammad Khayrat still stands on a small hill above the sea. The St. Martin's launch terminal, the border market, the twin temples at Balughat, Tekerghona beach and the border haats are the pieces of a full day here.

On the ground: Launch terminal for St. Martin's; Naf river border villages; Shah Parbat dargah and viewpoint; Twin temples of Ramu side; Cheap seafood and dried fish market. GHORA GHURI guides rate the border, village, pilgrimage character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Teknaf Town & Shah Parbat: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

name: St. Martin's Island
best_time: October-March only; the island closes to tourists in monsoon
short_description: St. Martin's is the country's most fragile and most loved sea destination: a small coral island with a walkable sandbar, limited water and no self-drive access. Two nights and a booked room make it work; one rushed day does not.
short_bn: নারিকেল ঝিঝিরা দেশের একমাত্র প্রবালময় দ্বীপ — জোয়ারের বালুচর, পরিষ্কার shallow পানি, নিষেধাজ্ঞা-মাফিক নির্মাণ আর গাছের ছায়া; দুই রাত আর আগে থেকে বুক করা ঘর না হলে ভ্রমণটা জমে না।
long_description:
St. Martin's is the country's most fragile and most loved sea destination: a small coral island with a walkable sandbar, limited water and no self-drive access. Two nights and a booked room make it work; one rushed day does not. Narikel Jinjira, Bangladesh's only coral-bearing island, ringed by clear shallow water and a palm-shaded sandbar a sixteen-kilometre boat ride offshore. The island council restricts building and bans plastic; only a few hundred visitors are handled comfortably, so pre-booked rooms are essential and day-trippers are the pressure point.

On the ground: Coral and clear shallows for snorkelling; Cheradi-side sandbar walk at low tide; Palm groves and fishing-village lanes; Restrictions on plastic and new construction; Fewer beds than demand, always. GHORA GHURI guides rate the island, beach, eco character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching St. Martin's Island: Cox's Bazar is 8-10 hours by non-stop bus (about 380 km), or 1 hour by air. Air: Cox's Bazar Airport, 15 minutes from the beach, with daily Dhaka flights. Ground links run through Cox's Bazar and Palongkhali bus stands; CNG and safari jeeps for the coast.

Staying over: expect beach-resort strip from Laboni to Sugandha, plus budget hotels near Krinojura Bazaar.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March only; the island closes to tourists in monsoon. Budget 4,000-14,000 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 2 day(s) on the ground. Everything arrives by boat, including supplies. Carry cash, expect early power cuts after midnight, and never plan a same-day return in uncertain weather.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with St. Martin's Island site authorities before travel. long_description:
Kaptai Lake is the heart of the Hill Tracts trip - a huge man-made water body of drowned ridges, boat villages and tribal markets. Two nights, one on the water and one in Rangamati town, is the minimum to enjoy it. A 680-square-kilometre人工 lake on the Karnafuli, drowned hills and village cemeteries under its water, ringed by boat jetties, marinas and an aquarium. The engine-boat network links Rangamati, Kaptai ghat, Rangapuni and the border checkpoints; the garden at the dam is the sunset point.

Staying over: expect water bungalows and lakeside cottages at Paraikhali and Rajban Vihara.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; monsoon for full reservoir colour. Budget 2,500-8,000 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 2 day(s) on the ground.

name: Rangamati Town, Rajban Vihara & Shapupara
best_time: October-March; the Biju and Magh festivals add colour
short_description: Rangamati is the practical base for Kaptai Lake and the Chakma heritage circuit: a monastery on a ridge, a lake-front market town and boat connections everywhere. Add one day for the border trips to Tuiling Domba and Boga.
short_bn: কাপ্তাই জেলার সদর রাঙ্গামাটি — রাজবন বিহারের চূড়া, হ্রদমুখী বাজার, আদিবাসী জাদুঘর আর সর্বত্র নৌকা-সংযোগ; তুইলিং ডোম্বা-বোগা লেকের জন্য এক দিন বাড়ান।
long_description:
Rangamati is the practical base for Kaptai Lake and the Chakma heritage circuit: a monastery on a ridge, a lake-front market town and boat connections everywhere. Add one day for the border trips to Tuiling Domba and Boga. The lake-side capital of the Chakma circle, where the Rajban Vihara monastery looks over the Kaptai backwaters and the town market sells hill bamboo craft. The monastery viewpoint, the circuit house jetty and the museum of tribal culture are all walkable or a short CNG ride from the hotel strip.

name: Ukhiya T.C. Border Market
best_time: October-March; Wednesday and Sunday are bazaar days
short_description: Ukhiya is the most interesting single market in Bangladesh for textile and craft buyers, running in a river clearing beside the Myanmar border. It pairs naturally with Bandarban's Nilgiri and Tindi para viewpoints.

long_description:
Ukhiya is the most interesting single market in Bangladesh for textile and craft buyers, running in a river clearing beside the Myanmar border. It pairs naturally with Bandarban's Nilgiri and Tindi para viewpoints. The border trade point on the Myanmar road, where every Thursday-Sunday the weekly market brings Marma, Mro, Tripura and Rakhine traders into the same clearing. Bamboo baskets, hill pepper, ginger, cane work and hand-woven cloth; the entry check post requires ID, and foreigners need the current CHT permit rules checked in advance.

On the ground: Weekly tribal market at the border; Hill pepper, ginger and cane crafts; Marma and Rakhine village setting; Naf-side river scenery; ID and permit checks at the bazaar. GHORA GHURI guides rate the border, village, shopping character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Ukhiya T.C. Border Market: Bandarban is 8-10 hours via Dhaka-Chattogram highway and Rowangchhari. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 3.5 hours onward. Ground links run through Chattogram Badar Ghat buses to Bandarban; jeep for trek heads.

Staying over: expect hillside cottages and camps at Nijhum Dweep and Bilkalukunja, plus simple hotels.

best_time: November-February for the sea of clouds; monsoon for the waterfall
short_description: Chandraket is the overnight trek that made Bandarban famous: a jeep to the road-head, an hour's climb to a meadow on the ridge, then tents, cloud and stars. Book a local crew - the last stretch has no signposts.
short_bn: আরাকান পাহাড়ের হাজার মিটার উঁচু চন্দ্রকেট — জীপে রাস্তার শেষ, এক ঘণ্টার চড়াই, তারপর মাঠে তাঁবু, মেঘের সাগর আর তারা। শেষ অংশে পথচিহ্ন নেই, তাই স্থানীয় দল ভাড়া করাই নিরাপদ।
long_description:

Book a local crew - the last stretch has no signposts. A thousand-metre shoulder of the Arakan range with an abandoned army post on top, reached by a hired jeep and an hour's climb. Tents on the old parade ground, no electricity, and a two-hour walk down to the river village below the escarpment - the classic overnight trek of the district.

On the ground: Sea of clouds from the ridge; Abandoned upazagata buildings for camping; Jeep-and-trek access from Bandarban; Ridge viewpoint on the walk-out; Zero light pollution for stars. name: Alinagar & Sopyari Pahaar
best_time: October-March; mornings for mist on the ridge
short_description: Alinagar layers Chakma royal ruins, a cave shrine and a ridge viewpoint twenty minutes above Ramgarh, in the part of the hills where the old circle system still shapes local identity.

long_description:
Alinagar layers Chakma royal ruins, a cave shrine and a ridge viewpoint twenty minutes above Ramgarh, in the part of the hills where the old circle system still shapes local identity. A hill capital of the former Chakma circle with a ruined royal palace, a temple and a cave-shrine, reached on a ridge road above the Kaptai backwater. The Sopyari Pahaar viewpoint and the Alinagar palace ruins are a twenty-minute walk apart; local guides from the union office are cheap and worth hiring.

On the ground: Chakma royal palace ruins; Cave shrine and temple on the ridge; Sopyari Pahaar viewpoints; Boat-and-jeep loop via Ramgarh; Tribal homestays in the union. GHORA GHURI guides rate the hill, heritage, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Alinagar & Sopyari Pahaar: Khagrachhari is 7-8 hours via Chattogram and Mahalchhari. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 2.5 hours onward. Ground links run through Chattogram buses to Khagrachhari; CNG to Chander Gari and the falls.

Staying over: expect eco-cottages at Chander Gari and simple town hotels near the clock tower.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; mornings for mist on the ridge. Budget 900-2,500 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Hill roads are narrow and mist is common; hire a local driver rather than a self-drive car, and carry a layer for every evening.

name: Tripura Kingdom Heritage
best_time: November-February; the Bishu festival in April
short_description: The Tripura heritage belt in Rangamati and Khagrachhari explains the hills as a living kingdom rather than scenery - palace mounds, temples, weavers and the Bishu festival calendar, all visitable with a community guide.
short_bn: রাঙ্গামাটি-খাগড়াছড়ির ত্রিপুরা ঐতিহ্য বেল্টে রাজবাড়ির স্তূপ, মন্দির, তাঁত আর বিষু-খার্চাই উৎসব — পাহাড়কে শুধু দৃশ্য না দেখে এক জীবন্ত রাজ্য হিসেবে বোঝার উপায়।
long_description:
The Tripura heritage belt in Rangamati and Khagrachhari explains the hills as a living kingdom rather than scenery - palace mounds, temples, weavers and the Bishu festival calendar, all visitable with a community guide. The remains of the Tripura rajas' seats - the palace mounds, royal cremation grounds and temples - scattered on the Indian side and the Bangladesh side of the old kingdom. On the Bangladesh side the sites cluster around Rangamati Sadar and Naniyachhar, visited best with a Tripura community guide; the language and craft trail continues at Khagrachhari.

On the ground: Rajbari and royal memorial mounds; Tripura temples and bamboo shrines; Bishu and Kharchai festival dates; Weaving and bamboo craft workshops; Community-guided village route. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, culture, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Tripura Kingdom Heritage: Rangamati is 7-8 hours via Chattogram and Kaptai Lake. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 2.5 hours onward. Ground links run through Chattogram-Dohazari buses, then engine boats across Kaptai Lake.

Staying over: expect water bungalows and lakeside cottages at Paraikhali and Rajban Vihara.

Planning notes: the season window is November-February; the Bishu festival in April. Budget 900-2,400 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Bring water, a hat and patience: most brick monuments are open, shaded by little more than their own arcades, and a guide reads the site far better than any plaque.

short_description: Chattogram's war cemetery is the country's largest Second World War burial ground, a Commonwealth garden holding the Burma campaign dead. It is short, moving, free and sits on the way into the city from the airport.
short_bn: বurma অভিযানের দ্বিতীয় বিশ্বযুদ্ধের ২,৭০০-র বেশি সমাধির কমনওয়েলথ গার্ডেনস - বিমানবন্দর পথেই, ছোট, গম্ভীর আর বিনামূল্যে দেখার জায়গা।
long_description:
Chattogram's war cemetery is the country's largest Second World War burial ground, a Commonwealth garden holding the Burma campaign dead. It is short, moving, free and sits on the way into the city from the airport. A Commonwealth War Graves cemetery for the Second World War dead of the Burma campaign, with more than 2,700 burials, set on a green slope near the airport road. The adjacent memorial, the graves of soldiers of many nations and the maintenance standard make it a stop of real weight for visitors tracing the 1942-45 frontier war.

name: Bayazid Bostami Shrine & Caves
best_time: October-March; Urs on 7-9 June draws the largest crowd
short_description: Bayazid Bostami gives Chattogram its oldest continuous sacred site: a hill shrine and cave hermitage above the city, still filled for the June urs. The climb takes twenty minutes and the port view is the best in town.
short_bn: পাহাড়ের গুহায় XI শতকের সূফী আউলিয়া বায়াজিদ বোস্তামির মাজার, প্রাকৃতিক ঝরনা আর জুন মাসের উরস; ওঠা বিশ মিনিট, আর চট্টগ্রাম বন্দরের সেরা দৃশ্য।
long_description:
Bayazid Bostami gives Chattogram its oldest continuous sacred site: a hill shrine and cave hermitage above the city, still filled for the June urs. The climb takes twenty minutes and the port view is the best in town. A Sufi shrine of the eleventh century set in a cave system above the town, with rock-cut cells, a natural spring and a two-day urs each June. The cave clusters, the graveyard terraces and the view over Chattogram's port make the climb worthwhile; the site stays active, so dress and behaviour matter.

On the ground: Eleventh-century Sufi dargah; Rock-cut cave cells and springs; June urs and lakh-strong gathering; Viewpoint over the port city; Ten-minute drive from Agrabad. GHORA GHURI guides rate the pilgrimage, heritage, cave character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Air: Shah Amanat International Airport with daily Dhaka and international flights. Ground links run through Dampara and Badar Ghat bus stands; Agrabad and Nasirabad for onward vans.

Andar Killa is the old fortification that still gives port-side Chattogram its historic core - a low rampart hill beside the shrine of a Sufi sailor, five minutes from the bazaar it was built to protect. The inner fort of old Chattogram, thrown up in 1792 by the East India Company after the Arakanese and Mughal contests for the port, on a low hill above the caravan lane. It stands fifteen minutes from New Market, next to the Shah Muhammad Sultan shrine, with a lighthouse nearby and the Karnaphuli ghat downhill.

short_description: Patenga combines a working sea beach, an abandoned war runway and a wall of ships on the horizon, ten minutes more than the drive from Agrabad. It is the sunset place for Chattogram families and for anyone with a late flight.
short_bn: কর্ণফুলীর মুখে পতেঙ্গা — বিমানবন্দর-রানওয়ে সমুদ্রের কিনারা ঘেঁষে চলে, সামনে জাহাজের সারি আর পাশে মাছের দোকান; বিকেল দেখার শহরের প্রিয় ঠিকানা।

It is the sunset place for Chattogram families and for anyone with a late flight. A beach reached along an old wartime runway that still runs within a hundred metres of the surf, facing the Karnaphuli mouth and the ship anchorage. The long walk to the quieter western end, the sea-face seafood stalls and the ship-line sunset make this the city beach; the runway itself is closed to vehicles.

On the ground: Second World War runway at the sea edge; Ship anchorage sunset line; Walk to the quieter western end; Seafood stalls and beach chairs; Twenty minutes from Agrabad. name: Chattogram Port, Agrabad & New Market
best_time: October-March; morning for crane-light, dusk for the ferry
short_description: Chattogram's port quarter is the country's economic engine and an underrated half day: colonial warehouses, a river ferry culture, the Karnaphuli tunnel and a bazaar grid that has traded with Arakan and Bengal for three centuries.
short_bn: চট্টগ্রামের বন্দর-আগ্রাবাদ অংশ দেশের অর্থনীতির ইঞ্জিন আর অবমূল্যায়িত আধা দিন — ঔপনিবেশিক গুদাম, নৌ-ফেরি, কর্ণফুলী টানেল আর তিন শতাব্দীর নিউমার্কেটের বাজারজাল।
long_description:
Chattogram's port quarter is the country's economic engine and an underrated half day: colonial warehouses, a river ferry culture, the Karnaphuli tunnel and a bazaar grid that has traded with Arakan and Bengal for three centuries. Bangladesh's main seaport and its warehouse architecture: the 1889 railway terminus, the Agrabad administrative blocks, the Karnaphuli river ferry and New Market's bazaar grid. The Agrabad warehouses, the Japanese Memorial and the Port Museum give the industrial story; the Karnaphuli tunnel and the Shah Amanat bridge close the loop.

On the ground: Working port and shipyard views; Karnaphuli tunnel and river ferry; Colonial warehouse architecture; New Market and Andarmeer lanes; Port museum and war memorials. GHORA GHURI guides rate the city, industrial, heritage character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Chattogram Port, Agrabad & New Market: Chattogram is 4.5-6 hours on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, or by train and launch. Air: Shah Amanat International Airport with daily Dhaka and international flights. Ground links run through Dampara and Badar Ghat bus stands; Agrabad and Nasirabad for onward vans.

Staying over: expect sea-view hotels on Koliana Ghat Road and heritage stays in Old Chattogram.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; morning for crane-light, dusk for the ferry. Budget 400-1,400 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Traffic, not distance, decides timing here. Group sites by neighbourhood and use ride-share or rickshaw between them rather than one long walk.

name: Charamba Zamindan Bari, Feni
best_time: October-March; mornings for empty courtyards
short_description: Charamba gives the Dhaka-Chattogram road its best heritage exit: a landlord township of palace, tank and temples twenty minutes off the highway, rarely visited and easy to combine with Noakhali or Cumilla.
short_bn: ফেনীর চরম্বা জমিদার বাড়ি — ঢাকা-চট্টগ্রাম মহাসড়ক থেকে কুড়ি মিনিট ভেতরে প্রাসাদ, পুকুর, মন্দির আর লাইব্রেরি-উপাংশ নিয়ে এক অল্প-দর্শক ঐতিহ্যস্থান।
long_description:
Charamba gives the Dhaka-Chattogram road its best heritage exit: a landlord township of palace, tank and temples twenty minutes off the highway, rarely visited and easy to combine with Noakhali or Cumilla. The palace complex of the Chowdhuries of Charamba, one of Feni's great nineteenth-century landlord houses, with a tank, temples and a library wing. It sits twenty minutes from Feni town on the Dhaka-Chattogram corridor, making it a legitimate stop rather than a detour for road travellers.

On the ground: Chowdhury palace and library wing; Palace tank and bathing ghats; Family temple row; Terracotta and plaster fronts; On the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, village, offbeat character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Charamba Zamindan Bari, Feni: Feni is 3.5-4.5 hours on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 1 hour; Cox's Bazar is 1.5 hours south. Ground links run through Feni bus stand and railway station on the Dhaka-Chattogram line.

Staying over: expect a few hotels in Sadar; most visitors pass through to Noakhali or Cox's Bazar.

name: Mainamati & Shalban Vihara
best_time: October-March; the site museum closes on Sundays
short_description: Mainamati, above Cumilla, is the archaeology that predates and pairs with Paharpur: a sultanate-and-before monastic city of brick stupas, wells and a great courtyard vihara, with a site museum that few visitors bother to enter.
short_bn: কুমিল্লার মাইনামতি — চন্দ্রবংশের বিক্রমপুর তথা বৌদ্ধ বিহার-নগরী; শালবন বিহারের ১১৫টি কক্ষ, গোকুল মেধের ইটের পিরামিড আর টেরাকোটার স্থানীয় জাদুঘর।
long_description:
Mainamati, above Cumilla, is the archaeology that predates and pairs with Paharpur: a sultanate-and-before monastic city of brick stupas, wells and a great courtyard vihara, with a site museum that few visitors bother to enter. The Chandra-dynasty capital of Vikramapura and its great Buddhist monastery complex - Shalban Vihara, the Gokul Medh, Rusru Medh and a museum of brick and terracotta. Twenty mounds are spread over the cantonment hills; the site museum's terracotta plaques are the best collection of the period in Bangladesh outside Paharpur.

On the ground: Shalban Vihara's 115-cell plan; Gokul Medh brick pyramid; Mainamati Site Museum; Chandra and Deva dynasty coins; Cantonment hill-side setting. GHORA GHURI guides rate the heritage, archaeology, world-heritage-candidate character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Mainamati & Shalban Vihara: Cumilla is 3.5-4.5 hours on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, or by train. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 1 hour. Ground links run through Cumilla bus stand and railway junction on the Dhaka-Chattogram-Sylhet spine.

Staying over: expect hotel blocks near Kandirpar and rest houses near Mainamati.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; the site museum closes on Sundays. Budget 350-1,100 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Bring water, a hat and patience: most brick monuments are open, shaded by little more than their own arcades, and a guide reads the site far better than any plaque.

name: Raipur Beach & Karnafuli Mouth
best_time: October-March; monsoon erosion changes the shoreline
short_description: Raipur is the Chattogram division's quiet water's-edge - an estuary beach of sandbars, ferry traffic and fish landings, close enough to the city for an evening and empty enough for a weekend.
short_bn: লক্ষ্মীপুরের রাইপুর — ধলেশ্বরী-কার্নাফুলীর সমুদ্রমুখের লম্বা অবিকসিত সৈকত, ফেরি-ট্রাফিক আর ভোরে মাছ অবতরণ; চট্টগ্রাম থেকে এক ঘণ্টায় নির্জন জলতীর।
long_description:
Raipur is the Chattogram division's quiet water's-edge - an estuary beach of sandbars, ferry traffic and fish landings, close enough to the city for an evening and empty enough for a weekend. The estuary beach where the Dhaleshwari and Karnafuli reach the Bay, with a long sand front, a ferry culture and no resort block at all. Local boats run to the char side; Raipur is also a fishing landing, so the morning catch, not the sunset, is the real show.

On the ground: Wide undeveloped estuary beach; Ferry and country-boat crossings; Morning catch at the landing; Historic river-port warehouses; One hour from Chattogram city. GHORA GHURI guides rate the beach, river, offbeat character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Raipur Beach & Karnafuli Mouth: Lakshmipur is 5-6 hours via Cumilla and Ramganj. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 1.5 hours. Ground links run through Lakshmipur and Ramganj bus stands, with vans to Raipur ghat.

Staying over: expect small guesthouses; Raipur and Cox's Bazar cover most overnight needs.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; monsoon erosion changes the shoreline. Budget 500-1,500 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. Sea conditions matter more than the calendar here - the surf is calm and swimmable only outside the monsoon, and tides decide how much sand is usable.

name: Chandpur Karnafuli Ghat
best_time: October-March; evenings for the launch traffic
short_description: Chandpur's riverfront is classic delta infrastructure - ghats, jetties and three rivers meeting - with the sultanate mosque at Haziganj as its heritage anchor. It makes a natural lunch stop on the Dhaka-Chattogram rail or road journey.
short_bn: চাঁদপুরের নদীতীরে মেঘনা-ধলেশ্বরী-কার্নাফুলীর মিলন, স্টিমার-লঞ্চ ঘাট আর হাজীগঞ্জের শাহবাজ খাঁ মসজিদ — ঢাকা-চট্টগ্রাম পথে থামার সেরা জায়গা।
long_description:
Chandpur's riverfront is classic delta infrastructure - ghats, jetties and three rivers meeting - with the sultanate mosque at Haziganj as its heritage anchor. It makes a natural lunch stop on the Dhaka-Chattogram rail or road journey. A river-port town where the Meghna, Dhaleshwari and Karnafuli braid together, keeping steamer ghats, a banyan-shaded old dock line and the gateway to Haziganj. Haziganj's Shahbaz Khan mosque, thirty minutes away, is the historical prize; the Chandpur launch terminal is how most of the delta's people still move.

On the ground: Three-river confluence riverfront; Historic steamer and launch ghats; Shahbaz Khan Mosque at Haziganj; Riverside jute warehouse lanes; Rail-connected town on the Dhaka line. GHORA GHURI guides rate the river, heritage, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Chandpur Karnafuli Ghat: Chandpur is 4-5 hours via Cumilla and Faridganj, or launch on the Dhaleshwari. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 1 hour. Ground links run through Chandpur bus stand, with a short rickshaw ride to the Karnafuli ghat.

Staying over: expect basic hotels near the court area, plus riverside resorts at Haziganj.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; evenings for the launch traffic. Budget 300-900 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. River levels rewrite the map every year: launch timetables, ghats and sandbanks all move. Build a buffer day into any river-based plan.

name: Noakhali Baor & Snighajer Wetland
best_time: November-February; monsoon floods submerge the roads
short_description: Noakhali's baor belt is a wetland landscape most itineraries skip, yet it offers winter birding, village boat travel and the delta's fishing economy at very low cost, within three hours of Dhaka.
short_bn: নোয়াখালী-লক্ষ্মীপুরের বাওর-বেল্ট — শীতের জলপাখি, ভাসমান চাষ, নৌকা-যোগাযোগ আর মাছ ধরার অর্থনীতি, ঢাকা থেকে তিন ঘণ্টার মধ্যেই পায়ের তলায়।
long_description:
Noakhali's baor belt is a wetland landscape most itineraries skip, yet it offers winter birding, village boat travel and the delta's fishing economy at very low cost, within three hours of Dhaka. A closed-delta lake system south of Dhaka's sprawl - the baors of Noakhali and Lakshmipur, where beel fishing, floating agriculture and winter birds still run village life. The beels along the Noakhali-Feni road hold winter waterfowl, and the run from Feni to Chat Khali gives the best of it in half a day.

On the ground: Winter birds on the closed beel; Beel fishing and floating farms; River-island villages and ferry points; Salt-tide landscape on the sea edge; Half an hour from Feni and Cumilla. GHORA GHURI guides rate the river, eco, village character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Noakhali Baor & Snighajer Wetland: Noakhali is 4-5 hours via Cumilla and the Noakhali bypass. Air: Shah Amanat (Chattogram), about 1.5 hours. Ground links run through Noakhali and Maijdee bus stands; vans to Snighajer and Sandwip ghats.

Staying over: expect town hotels and NGO guesthouses, with a growing set of sandbar resorts.

name: Srimangal Tea Country
best_time: October-March; April-June for the second flush
short_description: Srimangal is the gentlest multi-day trip in Bangladesh: tea gardens on every horizon, an eco-resort inside a rainforest, bamboo groves and a town built around the heritage railway. Two nights, one on an estate.
short_bn: শ্রীমঙ্গল দেশের সবচেয়ে শান্ত বহুদিবস ভ্রমণ — চারদিকে চাবাগান, লাউয়াছড়ার ইকো-রিসর্ট, বাঁশঝাড় আর ঐতিহাসিক রেলওয়ে টাউন; অন্তত এক রাত চা-বাগানের বঙলোতে কাটান।
long_description:
Srimangal is the gentlest multi-day trip in Bangladesh: tea gardens on every horizon, an eco-resort inside a rainforest, bamboo groves and a town built around the heritage railway. Two nights, one on an estate. The tea capital of Bangladesh, ringed by some ninety estates, with the vast Bisnakand estate on its doorstep and the Lawachara eco-resort inside a rainforest. The heritage Srimangal railway station, the tea museum and the Bisnakand border point are all within twenty minutes; estate bungalows are the best places to stay.

On the ground: Estate factory and tea-packing floor visits; Lawachara rainforest and hoolock gibbons; Bisnakand and Kalighat garden loops; Bamboo groves and mango orchards; Rail-connected town on the Dhaka-Sylhet line. GHORA GHURI guides rate the hill, eco, tea character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Srimangal Tea Country: Moulvibazar is 4.5-5.5 hours via Sylhet, or the direct bus from Sayedabad to Srimangal. Air: Osmani International Airport (Sylhet), about 1 hour onward. Ground links run through Srimangal and Moulvibazar bus stands; the railway station serves Chhatak Hill.

Staying over: expect tea gardens resorts - stay on an estate for the full experience.

Planning notes: the season window is October-March; April-June for the second flush. Budget 2,500-8,000 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 2 day(s) on the ground. Hill roads are narrow and mist is common; hire a local driver rather than a self-drive car, and carry a layer for every evening.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with Srimangal Tea Country site authorities before travel. name: Lawachara National Park
best_time: October-March; rain makes trails slippery but birds louder
short_description: Lawachara, above Kamalganj, is Bangladesh's premier lowland rainforest walk - a real canopy walk, gibbon mornings and overnight eco-cottages inside the park. It converts a tea trip into a genuine wildlife trip in one day.
short_bn: কামালগঞ্জের লাউয়াছড়া দেশের শ্রেষ্ঠ নিম্নভূমি বর্ষারণ্য — ক্যানোপি ওয়াক, হুলাক গিব্বন, লাইসেন্সপ্রাপ্ত গাইড আর বনের ভেতরেই রাত কাটানোর ইকো-রিসর্ট।
long_description:
Lawachara, above Kamalganj, is Bangladesh's premier lowland rainforest walk - a real canopy walk, gibbon mornings and overnight eco-cottages inside the park. It converts a tea trip into a genuine wildlife trip in one day. A 5,000-acre tropical rainforest with a canopy walk, the hoolock gibbon and one of Bangladesh's best night-stay arrangements inside a protected forest. Park entry requires a registered guide; the eco-resort inside the forest and the Kamalganj road make Srimangal the natural base.

On the ground: Canopy walk and eco-trail network; Hoolock gibbon and pheasant sightings; Licensed forest guides on entry; Rainforest eco-resort for overnight; Butterfly and medicinal-plant trails. GHORA GHURI guides rate the wildlife, eco, hill character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

name: Tangaur Taker Haor
best_time: December-February for birds; June-September for the flooded lake
short_description: Tangaur Haor floods into a lake and empties into grass, and both halves of that year are worth seeing. Birders come for the winter concentration; everyone else comes for the boat-and-horizon feeling no other Bangladeshi landscape gives.
short_bn: টাঙ্গুর-টেকের হাওড় বর্ষায় ৪,৪০০ হেক্টরের হ্রদ, শীতে ঘাস আর পাখির সমাবেশ — নৌকা, টापু-গ্রাম আর কমিউনিটির ইকো-ক্যাম্প, যে দৃশ্য অন্য কোথাও পাওয়া যায় না।
long_description:
Tangaur Haor floods into a lake and empties into grass, and both halves of that year are worth seeing. Birders come for the winter concentration; everyone else comes for the boat-and-horizon feeling no other Bangladeshi landscape gives. One of Bangladesh's largest haors, 4,400 hectares of seasonal lake studded with forested islands, home to a critically important winter bird congregation. Boats and a guide are arranged at the southern-edge ghat; the islands hold orchards and shrines, and there is a single community-run eco-camp at the northern end.

On the ground: Winter congregation of migratory ducks; Island villages and forest patches; Boat-only access from the ghat; Community eco-camp on the haor edge; Riverside villages and landing points. GHORA GHURI guides rate the haor, birding, island character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Tangaur Taker Haor: Habiganj is 5-6 hours via Sylhet and Madhabpur. Air: Osmani International Airport (Sylhet), about 1 hour. Ground links run through Habiganj and Madhabpur bus stands; shared vans to Madhabkunda falls.

Staying over: expect estate bungalows, Jaintia border homestays and simple hotels in Madhabpur.

Planning notes: the season window is December-February for birds; June-September for the flooded lake. Budget 1,800-4,500 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 2 day(s) on the ground. The haor floods completely from June to August; boat-dependent travel is only realistic from October to March, and the best birding window is December to February.

All rates, opening hours and transport times in this listing are indicative and should be confirmed with Tangaur Taker Haor site authorities before travel. best_time: Any month; the annual urs in Muharram is the huge one
short_description: Shah Jalal's dargah is why Sylhet is Sylhet - the shrine that anchored Islam's spread in the north-east, sitting above a city of water, tea and stone boats. Two hours here explains the division better than three days of drives.
short_bn: চতুর্দশ শতকের হযরত শাহ জালাল (র.)-এর মাজারই শহরের নাম আর পরিচয়ের উৎস; পাহাড়ে উঠে দক্ষিণ সুরমার দৃশ্য, নামতে দরগাহ মহল্লার পুরনো বাজার।
long_description:
Shah Jalal's dargah is why Sylhet is Sylhet - the shrine that anchored Islam's spread in the north-east, sitting above a city of water, tea and stone boats. Two hours here explains the division better than three days of drives. The fourteenth-century shrine of the patron saint of Sylhet on a hill above the old city, with the adjoining graveyard terraces and a bazaar winding up to the gate. Dargah Mahalla, the Ambarkhana road and the up-market lanes of South Surma are the walk down; keep phone cameras respectful inside the compound.

On the ground: Fourteenth-century Sufi shrine on a hill; Adjacent Shah Parbat tomb complex; Friday and urs crowd scale; Dargah Mahalla old bazaar lanes; Viewpoint over the city and river. name: Goylaghat & Jaintiapur Old Capital
best_time: November-February; monsoon closes the ford roads
short_description: Goylaghat-Jaintiapur is the north-east at its most scenic and least serviced: an old kingdom's mound by a wide river, boulder fields and waterfalls within reach, and roads that demand a proper vehicle and a local driver.
short_bn: গোয়াইনঘাট-জৈন্তাপুরে জৈন্তিয়া রাজ্যের স্মৃতি, প্রশস্ত নদীর পাথুরে ঘাট, ডোলিংরুপাই পাথরমালা আর পাতারিকুচির ঝরনা - শেষ কিলোমিটারগুলোতে জীপ বা মোটরসাইকেল ছাড়া চলে না।
long_description:
Goylaghat-Jaintiapur is the north-east at its most scenic and least serviced: an old kingdom's mound by a wide river, boulder fields and waterfalls within reach, and roads that demand a proper vehicle and a local driver. The old capital of the Jaintia kings on the Goai river, with a palace mound, a temple and the border hills of India across a wide stony river. The Harigad earthworks, the Dolingrupai boulder bed and the seasonal border waterfalls lie in the same upazila; all need a 4x4 or a motorbike for the last kilometres.

name: Jagannath Temple, Sunamganj
best_time: November-February; Rath Yatra is the festival to plan for
short_description: Sunamganj's Jagannath temple is one of eastern Bengal's most important standing Hindu monuments, still pulling a huge Rath Yatra crowd. It is the heritage anchor for a division otherwise sold entirely on haors and falls.

Sunamganj's Jagannath temple is one of eastern Bengal's most important standing Hindu monuments, still pulling a huge Rath Yatra crowd. It is the heritage anchor for a division otherwise sold entirely on haors and falls. A seventeenth-century brick temple on a hill above the Sunai river, the 'little Jagannath' of eastern Bengal, with terracotta panels and a great annual car festival. The temple hill, the museum of the district and the boat point to Boalakhum lie within an hour, making this the anchor of a Sunamganj day.

name: Boalakhum Wetland
best_time: June-September for the drowned forest; October for clear water
short_description: Boalakhum works only in its own season: between July and October a submerged forest you can boat through, in December a green field. It is Sunamganj's signature image and the strongest reason to time a haor trip carefully.
short_bn: বোয়ালখুম ঋতুর জায়গা — জুলাই-অক্টোবরে ডুবে যাওয়া বনের মাঝ দিয়ে নৌকা, ডিসেম্বরে সবুজ মাঠ; সুনামগঞ্জের সবচেয়ে পরিচিত ছবি আর সময়-নির্বাচনের কঠিন প্রশ্ন।
long_description:
Boalakhum works only in its own season: between July and October a submerged forest you can boat through, in December a green field. It is Sunamganj's signature image and the strongest reason to time a haor trip carefully. A haor that drowns a grove each monsoon, so that in the high water a boat runs between half-submerged trees - the country's most photographed flooded landscape. Reached by boat from the Dwaribazar landing; there is no resort infrastructure, only village rooms, so plan a Sunamganj base and a one-way boat.

On the ground: Boating among submerged trees; Seasonal lake that vanishes in winter; Otter and river-dolphin sighting reports; Village-room stays, zero resorts; One hour from Sunamganj town. GHORA GHURI guides rate the haor, boat, eco character of this place as the main reason to build a stop around it.

Reaching Boalakhum Wetland: Sunamganj is 6-7 hours via Sylhet and Chhatak, or launch from Khalia Juri. Air: Osmani International Airport (Sylhet), about 2 hours onward. Ground links run through Sunamganj bus stand; engines and launches cross the haors.

Planning notes: the season window is June-September for the drowned forest; October for clear water. Budget 700-2,200 BDT per person for a standard guided visit, and allow 1 day(s) on the ground. The haor floods completely from June to August; boat-dependent travel is only realistic from October to March, and the best birding window is December to February.
